page_title: Build a Realtime Serverless GraphQL API with Websockets on AWS

sources.entry: Build A Realtime Serverless GraphQL API with WebSockets on AWS

summary.title: Build a Realtime Serverless GraphQL API with Websockets on AWS
summary.one_liner: You learn to deploy a GraphQL subscription API on AWS AppSync using local resolvers (no database or Lambda) and consume its realtime websocket updates from Node.js and browser clients written in vanilla JavaScript.
keywords: how to build realtime api serverless
takeaways: AppSync local resolvers with a NONE data source can relay mutations to live subscribers without a database or Lambda function.
The @aws_subscribe directive ties a subscription field to a mutation so clients receive pushed updates over websockets.
The Serverless Framework and serverless-appsync-plugin provision the AppSync API, schema, and VTL mapping templates with one deploy command.
A single isomorphic JavaScript codebase using aws-appsync can run in Node.js (via babel) or in the browser (via webpack).
summary.summary: The tutorial explains that AWS AppSync now enables realtime serverless apps, since Lambda cannot hold websocket connections. It walks through writing a GraphQL schema with a Message mutation and an inbox subscription, VTL request and response mapping templates using a local resolver, and deploying with the Serverless Framework and serverless-appsync-plugin. It then builds an isomorphic vanilla JavaScript client using aws-appsync and shows how to run it in Node.js with babel and in the browser with webpack-dev-server, triggering updates from the AppSync console. The full source is linked on GitHub.
